time.expression: T_reduce(m, δ); m ≈ sqrt(n log₂(q) / log₂(δ))

space.expression: Depends on the selected lattice-reduction algorithm.

notes: Early explicit dual-LWE geometry model. Shortness and dimension predictions do not supply a universal LWE running-time exponent.

extra.parameters: Prime q=q(n); secret dimension n; root-Hermite factor δ; choose m only when enough samples are available.
extra.noise: Rounded Gaussian width αq; continuous standard deviation αq/√(2π).
extra.samples: At least m ≈ √(n log₂ q / log₂ δ); cap m by the actual sample budget.
extra.objective: Distinguish LWE from uniform using a short dual vector.
extra.model: Unscaled dual length ≈ q⁻¹ min(q, 2^{2√(n log₂(q) log₂(δ))}); source Eqs. (10)–(11).
extra.assumptions: Empirical lattice-reduction quality model for random q-ary lattices.
extra.success: Non-negligible distinguishing signal requires suitably small αq·||w||; no common fixed advantage is imposed here.

space.expression: Depends on the chosen SVP oracle inside BKZ.

notes: Historical dual model combining target vector length with a stated BKZ oracle. Its rule-of-thumb relation β/log₂β≈1/(2log₂δ₀) avoids falsely extrapolating an empirical seconds fit into a subexponential LWE algorithm.

extra.parameters: Fix n,q(n), Gaussian width αq, target one-vector bias ε and BKZ cost model; enough samples for optimized m.
extra.noise: Discrete Gaussian width αq, standard deviation αq/√(2π).
extra.samples: Unlimited samples in this historical survey; m≈√(nlog₂q/log₂δ₀) per fresh dual-vector instance, repeated for amplification.
extra.objective: Distinguish LWE from uniform with constant final advantage.
extra.model: ||v||≈δ₀^m q^{n/m}; bias≈exp(−π(α||v||)²); β/log₂β≈1/(2log₂δ₀). Select the SVP-oracle cost explicitly.
extra.assumptions: Lattice-reduction/Gaussian heuristic model and independent repetitions.
extra.success: One-vector bias ε; O(ε⁻²) independent observations for constant final advantage.

space.expression: Reduced basis plus M short dual vectors, if stored.

notes: Reuses an expensive reduced basis to generate many shorter dual relations. The claimed reduction relies on relations being sufficiently short and sufficiently random; fixed-sample correlations remain a heuristic.

extra.parameters: Fix n,q, Gaussian width αq, lattice dimension m, block sizes β,β′ and required relation count M.
extra.secret: General LWE secret; this amortization does not require a short secret.
extra.samples: Works on the available LWE matrix; reuses it, unlike fully independent fresh-sample amplification.
extra.model: One BKZ-β preprocessing followed by sparse unimodular rerandomization and cheaper BKZ-β′; source instantiation β′=2.
extra.assumptions: Cheap rerandomization yields short, adequately random relations; dependence can be ignored in the statistical test.
extra.success: Target advantage determines M; source estimates use dual-vector norm inflation by a factor of two.
